Underground Subway History

Fact #1

The First Underground Railway

The world’s first underground passenger railway opened in London in 1863. Its trains were powered by steam locomotives, long before modern electric subway systems.

Fact #2

A Deep Underground Milestone

London’s City & South London Railway opened in 1890. It used electric trains in deep tunnels beneath the city, helping establish the model for later deep-level subway lines.

Fact #3

Budapest Goes Underground

Budapest’s Millennium Underground opened in 1896. It was the first underground electric railway on continental Europe, and part of the original line is still in service today.

Current Competition

Subway Glide

Drone navigation • 15-second standard run • Two build groups

The goal is to travel the greatest possible distance through your own tunnel setup during a standard 15-second run.

Challenge Description

Design and build a drone capable of navigating through a passage with an opening of 18" × 18" without touching any of the drones. Participants are responsible for making their own tunnel setup. Every official attempt uses the same 15-second time limit. The challenge is to see how far your drone can get before time runs out.

Rules & Safety

  • Passage size: The tunnel passage opening must measure 18 inches × 18 inches.
  • Course: Each participant must make and provide their own tunnel setup.
  • Objective: Navigate through the passage without touching any of the drones and travel as far as possible.
  • Standard time: Each scored attempt is 15 seconds.
  • Scoring: The score is the distance traveled during the 15-second attempt. Include the measurement unit with your result.
  • Two build groups: Enter either Modified Drone or From Scratch Drone. This gives students a way to participate even if they do not have access to soldering equipment.
  • Verification: Record the full attempt clearly so the course, drone movement, 15-second timing, and distance can be reviewed by the Abacistics team.
  • Safety: Keep the course clear of people and fragile objects. Follow the drone manufacturer's safety guidance and have an adult supervise testing.

Build Groups

Modified Drone

For students starting with an existing drone and modifying it for the Subway Glide challenge. This group is intended to keep the competition accessible without requiring every participant to solder or build all electronics from scratch.

From Scratch Drone

For students designing and assembling their drone from scratch, including the additional electronics work involved in a full build.

Submission Process

To complete an official entry, students must submit:

  1. Division selection (Lower or Upper Elementary).
  2. Drone build group (Modified Drone or From Scratch Drone).
  3. Student first name, region, country, and project title.
  4. Distance traveled during the 15-second attempt, including units.
  5. A video link showing the complete run and the participant-built tunnel setup.
  6. Parent/guardian display consent.

Reminder for Parents

Parents are encouraged to assist with supervision, safe tool use, setup, and filming, but students should lead the design decisions and building process. Because drone electronics can be complex, choose the build group that matches the student's available tools, experience, and support.

General Rule:

"Ask your kid if they think it's cheating. They are generally pretty good at knowing."

If you are unsure if an action violates this guideline, email us at Abacistics.admin@gmail.com.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

What is the difference between the two build groups?

Modified Drone is for students adapting an existing drone. From Scratch Drone is for students building their drone from scratch. The two groups help make participation possible even when students do not have access to soldering.

Can I submit an improved attempt?

Yes. You can submit an updated video and result if you improve your project, subject to the competition's submission deadline.

Can I submit my project before the leaderboard goes live?

Yes! Early submissions are greatly appreciated because they give our staff a more spread-out timeline for reviewing projects. Please note that submissions received before the launch will not appear on the leaderboard until the listed launch date.

About Abacistics

We are a group of high school and college students dedicated to making hands-on engineering accessible, engaging, and welcoming for younger students.

We created Abacistics to bridge that gap. By offering focused, friendly challenges, we aim to inspire the next generation of builders, problem solvers, and innovators early on. We have all had transformative experiences through engineering, and we hope that through Abacistics, you will too.

Abacistics

A student-led STEM initiative making hands-on engineering challenges accessible and exciting for young builders.
